---
title: "Dangling References Prevented at Compile Time"
---

# Dangling References Prevented at Compile Time
In languages with manual memory management, creating a pointer to memory that has been deallocated results in a **dangling reference**. Rust guarantees this never occurs:

```rust
// Attempting to return a reference to a local variable:
// fn dangle() -> &String {
//     let s = String::from("temporary");
//     &s // ERROR: `s` does not live long enough
// }

// The idiomatic solution: transfer ownership of the value itself
fn no_dangle() -> String {
    let s = String::from("valid data");
    s
}

fn main() {
    let result = no_dangle();
    println!("Received: {}", result);
}
```
